'''Stojan Radenović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Стојан Раденовић}}; born 9 March 1948) is a [[Serbia]]n academic and politician. An internationally respected [[mathematician]], he has served in Serbia's [[National Assembly of Serbia|national assembly]] since 2022 as an independent representative endorsed by the [[Serbian Progressive Party]] (SNS). He was acting [[president of the National Assembly of Serbia|president of the assembly]] from February to March 2024.

==Early life and academic career==
Radenović was born in the village of [[Dobra Voda, Bojnik|Dobra Voda]] in the municipality of [[Bojnik, Serbia|Bojnik]], in what was then the [[People's Republic of Serbia]] in the [[Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia]]. He received a [[Ph.D.]] in 1979 and taught for the next two decades at the [[University of Kragujevac]] Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics. From 2000 to 2013, he was a full professor at the [[University of Belgrade]] Faculty of Mechanical Engineering.

In 2016, Radenović was personally responsible for the University of Belgrade ranking in the world's top three hundred universities for the first time on the prestigious [[Academic Ranking of World Universities|Shanghai list]], due to his large number of published works and citations. This accomplishment brought him to the attention of the wider public.<ref>[https://www.vreme.com/vreme/za-istrazivanje-granice-ne-postoje/ Slobodan Bubnjević, "Za istraživanje granice ne postoje"], ''Vreme'', 1 September 2016, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref><ref>[https://www.danas.rs/ljudi/stojan-radenovic-skromni-matematicar/ Vesna Andrić, "Stojan Radenović: Skromni matematičar"], ''Danas'', 24 August 2019, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref>

==Politician==
In the [[2022 Serbian parliamentary election]], the Serbian Progressive Party reserved the lead positions on its ''[[Together We Can Do Everything]]'' electoral list for non-party cultural figures and academics.<ref>[https://www.blic.rs/vesti/politika/ovako-vucic-kroji-vrh-izborne-liste-sns-sta-naprednjacima-donose-danica-grujicic-i/1xdqge0 "OVAKO VUČIĆ KROJI VRH IZBORNE LISTE SNS"], ''Blic'', 14 February 2022, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref> Radenović was given the second position on the list; this was [[tantamount to election]], and he was indeed elected when the list won a plurality victory with 120 out of 250 mandates.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori22/ko-su-kandidati-sns-za-narodne-poslanike/ "Ko su kandidati SNS za narodne poslanike?"], ''Danas'', 17 February 2022, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref> During the campaign, he credited the SNS with improving conditions in Serbia over its decade in power.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori22/profesor-radenovic-ponosan-sam-sto-sam-na-listi-sns-postao-sam-deo-istorije/ "Profesor Radenović: Ponosan sam što sam na listi SNS, postao sam deo istorije"], ''Danas'', 19 February 2022, accessed 17 April 2022.</ref> In his first term, Radenović was a member of the education committee{{efn|Formally known as the Committee on Education, Science, Technological Development, and the Information Society.}} and the subcommittee on science and higher education.<ref>[http://www.parlament.gov.rs/STOJAN_RADENOVIC.1180.488.html STOJAN RADENOVIC], {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006213859/http://www.parlament.gov.rs/STOJAN_RADENOVIC.1180.488.html |date=6 October 2022 }}, National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, 6 October 2022, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref><ref>[http://www.parlament.gov.rs/national-assembly/composition/working-bodies/subcommittees.493.html Subcommittees], {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230523123617/http://www.parlament.gov.rs/national-assembly/composition/working-bodies/subcommittees.493.html |date=23 May 2023 }}, National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, 23 May 2023, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref>

He was given the ninth position on the SNS's list in the [[2023 Serbian parliamentary election|2023 parliamentary election]] and was re-elected when the list won a majority victory with 129 seats.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/izbori-2023-kandidati-izborna-lista-srbija-ne-sme-da-stane-aleksandar-vucic/ "Pogledajte ko su kandidati na Vučićevoj listi Srbija ne sme da stane"], ''Danas'', 3 November 2023, accessed 29 March 2024.</ref> As the oldest member of the new parliament, Radenović was chosen as interim president when the assembly convened in February 2024.<ref>[https://www.danas.rs/vesti/politika/sta-je-rekao-stojan-radenovic-u-intervjuu-na-koji-je-reagovao-vladimir-obradovic/ "Šta je rekao Stojan Radenović u intervjuu na koji je reagovao Vladimir Obradović?"], ''Danas'', 12 February 2024, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref> He served in this role until 20 March, when [[Ana Brnabić]] was elected to the position.<ref>[https://www.politika.rs/sr/clanak/605056/Ana-Brnabic-izabrana-za-predsednicu-Narodne-skupstine#google_vignette "Ana Brnabić izabrana za predsednicu Narodne skupštine"], ''Politika'', 20 March 2024, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref>

He is now once again a member of the assembly's education committee.<ref>[http://www.parlament.gov.rs/STOJAN_RADENOVIC.1180.488.html STOJAN RADENOVIC], National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, accessed 3 April 2024.</ref>
